title: The strict density bound for monochromatic k-in-a-row on the integer grid
statement:
Let $D(k,\mathbb{Z}^2)$ denote the maximum density of a subset of the integer grid avoiding the relevant $k$-in-a-row configurations, and let $3\mathbb{N}$ denote the positive multiples of $3$. **Strict grid-density conjecture.** For every $k\in 3\mathbb{N}$,

$$
D(k,\mathbb{Z}^2)<1-\frac{2}{k}.
$$

The source establishes the corresponding upper bound $D(k,\mathbb{Z}^2)\leq 1-2/k$ and reports strictness for $k=3$ and computational evidence for $k=6$; the conjecture remains open in general.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.12880

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2026). “For small values of $k$, the conjecture has been verified in several cases , while it remains open in general.”
source_name: Kuo-Han Ku, “Monochromatic k in a row”, arXiv:2606.12880 (2026).
